cohort: The study included 150 conveniently selected pregnant women in Bangladesh during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: A high prevalence of depression (86.7%), anxiety (78.0%), and stress (75.3%) was found among pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic.
mod_finding: Stress was higher among those with no history of normal or caesarean section, while anxiety was higher in those with a history of normal birth and no history of caesarean section.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, within the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.
gest_age: Gestational age was considered, with early gestation being associated with higher anxiety.
